name: Conversion Copy Catalyst
tagline: 340 prompts that turn bland drafts into revenue copy
description: A 340-prompt library engineered for one outcome: copy that converts. Every prompt is tuned for GPT-5, Claude, and Gemini with role, context, and constraint slots, so the output lands on-brand the first time. Includes email sequences, ad angles, landing page sections, and a rewrite ladder that escalates from conservative to daring.
features: Prompt concepts across copy missions including headlines, email, ads, landing pages, onboarding, retention, and outbound
Model-tuned system scaffolds for GPT-5, Claude 4.x, and Gemini 2.x with temperature guidance
Brand-voice calibration worksheet concept to help align tone and terminology
Rewrite ladder concept with graduated edit levels, from polish to repositioning
Annotated swipe-file concept for studying how different prompt structures affect output
includes: Lifetime updates — new prompts added quarterly

faqs.q: Which AI models work with this pack?
faqs.a: Every prompt ships with model-specific scaffolds for GPT-5, Claude 4.x, and Gemini 2.x. They also run cleanly on open models like Llama and Mistral with minor temperature tweaks.

faqs.q: Can I use the output for client work?
faqs.a: Yes — the Extended License covers unlimited client projects and agencies. The Personal License covers one seat and your own projects.

faqs.q: How is this different from free prompt lists?
faqs.a: Each prompt is a system with roles, constraints, and iteration logic — not one-liners. The rewrite ladder alone typically saves 6–8 drafting rounds per asset.

faqs.q: Does this replace an SEO tool?
faqs.a: No — it complements one. The pack generates briefs, clusters, and optimizations; you still bring keyword volumes from your favorite tool.

faqs.q: Is it useful for programmatic SEO?
faqs.a: Yes. The brief generator includes templated-page patterns with unique-intent variants, a common programmatic SEO workflow.

faqs.q: What format is the calendar generator?
faqs.a: A prompt + Notion template combo: run the prompt, paste the output, and the Notion view auto-groups by week and content type.

faqs.q: Does it work for non-English stories?
faqs.a: Yes — prompts are language-agnostic. Add your target language as a constraint slot and the models follow it cleanly.

faqs.q: Can I use it for game writing?
faqs.a: Yes. Scene-tension prompts can branch into quest beats and NPC dialogue trees for game-writing workflows.

faqs.q: Is the output publishable as-is?
faqs.a: Treat it as a strong first draft. The pack's rewrite ladder prompts exist precisely to push AI output toward your voice.

faqs.q: Do the prompts touch my data warehouse?
faqs.a: No. Everything runs in your chat window; you paste schemas and results. Nothing leaves your tools.

faqs.q: Does it support dbt?
